# Administrator Environment Variable Reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-env-reference.py; do not edit. -->

From the **647** runtime configuration items of the [Environment Variable Reference](environment-variables-reference.md), this file
selects **176** variables administrators need to understand or approve, classified by responsibility.
The complete machine inventory remains the authoritative full set; this document does not list test, performance driver and purely internal pass-through variables.

## Reading Conventions

- The **regional manifest value** comes from `deploy/control-plane/regional/generated/`;
  `—` means the variable is not injected directly by a control-plane role ConfigMap/Secret and usually comes from
  `site.yaml`, the node installer, a data-plane Secret or an administrator command.
- The **application default/requirement** comes from the current Python implementation; `<required>` means missing equals failure,
  `<implicit>` means it is decided indirectly by higher-level configuration, dynamic names or a validator.
- Variables whose value type can be uniquely inferred from the code (see the `类型` column of the
  [Environment Variable Reference](environment-variables-reference.md)) are validated at process startup; a value of the wrong type will not go live with a process that looks healthy.
  Switch-type variables accept only `0/1/true/false/yes/no/on/off`, and must use the enabling word that switch itself
  recognises -- otherwise startup fails instead of silently staying off.
- In regional production do not use `kubectl set env` to temporarily override generated values; after changing the source of truth re-render,
  run `make docs-check`, then deploy per the release process.
- `GPU_FAULT_TEST_*`, `GPU_FAULT_PERF_*` and fleet transport temporary variables are not production
  service configuration and are not in this document.

## 1. Deployment Mode, Roles and Stable Identity

These variables decide which deployment mode, role and site a process belongs to. Regional production values should be generated by site.yaml, the renderer and the release state; administrators should not override them online.

| Environment variable | Regional manifest value | Application default/requirement | Meaning and management advice |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GPU_FAULT_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` | regional (the only production mode) | `'', 'single-cluster'` | Deployment mode. Production is fixed at regional; single-cluster is only for historical migration and local tests. |
| `GPU_FAULT_SERVICE_ROLE` | ingress=`ingress`<br>worker=`worker`<br>spool=`spool-worker` | `'all'` | Control-plane role: ingress only enqueues, worker consumes and orchestrates, spool-worker is the spool dedicated to consuming telemetry data. |
| `GPU_FAULT_SITE_ID` | `Secret gpu-fault-email/site-id` (three roles) | `<implicit>` | Stable site identifier, used for resource ownership, notification context and cross-release correlation; do not rename after creation. |
| `GPU_FAULT_AWS_REGION` | Injected from spec.awsRegion of site.yaml | `<implicit>` | AWS Region. CPU/GPU ARNs, Aurora, NLB, SES and monitoring resources must be in this Region. |
| `GPU_FAULT_CLUSTER_ID` | Injected per GPU cluster by the connection Secret/node installer | `<required>` | Stable ID of the managed GPU cluster; part of the isolation key of all resources, events, leases and actions. |
| `GPU_FAULT_RUNTIME_PROFILE_VERSION` | Content-addressed version generated by release-deploy | `<implicit>` | Immutable Runtime Profile version; Collector, Watcher, Agent and control plane must agree. |
| `GPU_FAULT_RELEASE_ID` | Injected from dist/current-release.json | `'', 'local'` | Release identifier, only for release tracking; the actual code identity is the wheel SHA and module_digest. |
| `GPU_FAULT_REGIONAL_CLUSTERS_JSON` | Generated from the regional registry ConfigMap/Secret | `''` | Bootstrap/disaster-recovery copy of the regional cluster registry; the runtime authoritative version is in the Aurora revision. |
| `GPU_FAULT_REGISTRY_POLL_SECONDS` | 1 | `'1'` | Period at which CPU processes poll the durable registry head. |
| `GPU_FAULT_REGISTRY_STALE_SECONDS` | 90 | `'10'` | When the registry has not refreshed successfully for longer than this, readiness and cluster-token requests fail closed. |
| `GPU_FAULT_UNKNOWN_ENV_POLICY` | — | `'error'` | Policy when an unknown GPU_FAULT_* variable is found. Production keeps error so typos do not silently take effect. |
| `GPU_FAULT_ALLOW_SINGLE_CLUSTER` | false (must not be enabled in production) | `False` | Explicit confirmation switch allowing a historical single-cluster active executor; must not be set in regional production. |

## 2. Credentials, TLS and Network Boundary

Credentials are injected only through Secrets, Secrets Manager or controlled files. Any plaintext, cross-cluster reuse, curl -k or proxy-forged loopback breaks the trust boundary.

| Environment variable | Regional manifest value | Application default/requirement | Meaning and management advice |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GPU_FAULT_EXECUTION_TOKEN` | CPU Secret; at least 32 characters | `''` | Administrator and control-plane internal operator credential; must not be distributed to the GPU data plane. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_REPLAY_SECRET` | CPU Secret; at least 32 characters and must differ from the execution token | `''` | Processor loopback replay credential; only a direct loopback peer is accepted. |
| `GPU_FAULT_CONTROL_PLANE_URL` | HTTPS URL injected by each cluster's connection Secret and the node installer | `<required>` | Stable URL through which the GPU data plane reaches the regional control plane; DNS, SAN and CA must be verified. |
| `GPU_FAULT_CONTROL_PLANE_TOKEN` | Independent Secret/node env per cluster | `<required>` | cluster token used by Collector, Watcher, Executor and Agent; must not be reused across clusters. |
| `GPU_FAULT_CONTROL_PLANE_CA_FILE` | Read-only CA public key file on the GPU data plane | `<implicit>` | Control-plane TLS trust root; bypassing with curl -k or verify=false is forbidden. |
| `GPU_FAULT_NODE_ACTION_KEYS_JSON` | CPU/GPU node key map Secret | `GPU_FAULT_NODE_ACTION_SECRETS_JSON, empty when unset` | Node-specific HMAC key map; each node uses only its own derived key. |
| `GPU_FAULT_NODE_ACTION_KEY_VERSION` | Node installer writes the current key version | `'1'` | Node action key version; advanced together with the required version and Agent generation during rotation. |
| `GPU_FAULT_REQUIRED_NODE_ACTION_KEY_VERSION` | `ConfigMap gpu-fault-release-metadata/required-node-action-key-version` (three roles) | `2 (when the Agent Registry is enabled)` | Node action key version accepted by the control plane; do not raise before the Fleet has converged. |
| `GPU_FAULT_NODE_AGENT_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT` | false; forbidden in regional production | `False` | Compatibility switch for isolated development environments only; the production installer generates the TLS cert/key automatically. |
| `GPU_FAULT_NODE_AGENT_TLS_CERT` | Generated automatically by the node installer, public certificate published via the signed heartbeat | `''` | Node Agent server certificate; the control plane verifies against the certificate pin in the heartbeat. |
| `GPU_FAULT_NODE_AGENT_TLS_KEY` | Node 0600 private key file | `''` | Node Agent server private key; must not enter ConfigMaps, logs or build artefacts. |
| `GPU_FAULT_NODE_AGENT_TLS_CLIENT_CA` | — | `''` | When configured requires Node Agent mTLS; when empty still relies on HMAC and the network boundary. |
| `GPU_FAULT_AGENT_ENDPOINT_ALLOWED_CIDRS` | Single-cluster/Canary compatibility path only; regional mode uses the per-cluster registration field | `''` | Single-cluster Agent endpoint CIDRs; regional mode reads agentEndpointAllowedCidrs by cluster_id. |
| `GPU_FAULT_AGENT_ENDPOINT_REQUIRE_TLS` | true | `True` | Requires the Agent endpoint to use HTTPS and the signed heartbeat to carry the server certificate. |

## 3. Store, Aurora and PostgreSQL

Regional production uses the Aurora PostgreSQL writer. The schema is managed by an independent ensure Job, business Pods only validate read-only; pool values are computed per Uvicorn process.

| Environment variable | Regional manifest value | Application default/requirement | Meaning and management advice |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GPU_FAULT_STORE_URL` | writer DSN from the gpu-fault-aurora Secret | `''` | State store connection. Regional production must be the PostgreSQL/Aurora writer; per-Pod SQLite cannot be used. |
| `GPU_FAULT_POSTGRES_AUTO_SCHEMA_INIT` | `false` (three roles) | `False` | Whether business processes run DDL themselves. Fixed false for the three regional roles; true only in development environments. |
| `GPU_FAULT_POSTGRES_HOT_STATE_MODE` | `dedicated` (three roles) | `'dedicated'` | Hot-state read/write mode. Production is dedicated; during migration advance legacy→dual→dedicated. |
| `GPU_FAULT_POSTGRES_POOL_MIN_SIZE` | `2` (three roles) | `'1'` | Minimum connections per process; the total connection budget must also be multiplied by Uvicorn processes and Pod replicas. |
| `GPU_FAULT_POSTGRES_POOL_MAX_SIZE` | ingress=`40`<br>worker=`24`<br>spool=`12` | `8 (PostgresStore); bare default 4 in the configuration preflight` | Maximum connections per process; must satisfy the Aurora limit and completion concurrency. |
| `GPU_FAULT_POSTGRES_POOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `10` (three roles) | `'2'` | Pool checkout timeout; a timeout becomes a capacity error instead of blocking the event loop. |
| `GPU_FAULT_POSTGRES_POOL_MAX_IDLE_SECONDS` | `300` (three roles) | `'300'` | Idle connection reclaim time, limiting long-idle connections. |
| `GPU_FAULT_POSTGRES_POOL_MAX_LIFETIME_SECONDS` | `3600` (three roles) | `'3600'` | Maximum connection lifetime, supporting credential rotation and network state refresh. |
| `GPU_FAULT_POSTGRES_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | — | `'540'` | Total statement timeout of the schema ensure; applies only to the migration Job. |
| `GPU_FAULT_POSTGRES_BOOTSTRAP_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | — | `'60'` | Upper bound for the schema ensure waiting on a relation/advisory lock. |
| `GPU_FAULT_POSTGRES_FLEET_CONNECTION_BUDGET` | ingress=`1200` | `<implicit>` | Database connection budget gate for all processes of the regional control plane; must be recomputed before scaling replicas or workers. |

## 4. Processor Capacity, Queues and Thread Pools

These values decide the regional queue capacity and per-process concurrency. Production values differ per role; they cannot be estimated from Pod count alone and must be multiplied by Uvicorn processes per Pod.

| Environment variable | Regional manifest value | Application default/requirement | Meaning and management advice |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_MODE` | `active-active` (three roles) | `'direct'` | Processor mode. Regional production is active-active; direct is only for the local path. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_WORKERS` | worker=`24` | `'4'` | Total processing slots per active worker process; the regional worker has 24. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_FAULT_WORKERS` | worker=`4` | `max(1, PROCESSOR_WORKERS // 4)` | Number of priority 0 fault pool workers, protecting XID/SXID and control requests. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_GPU_TELEMETRY_WORKERS` | worker=`4` | `max(1, PROCESSOR_WORKERS // 4)` | Number of GPU inventory/metrics pool workers. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_HOST_TELEMETRY_WORKERS` | worker=`4` | `max(1, PROCESSOR_WORKERS // 4)` | Number of Host telemetry/node-log pool workers. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_OBSERVATION_WORKERS` | worker=`2` | `max(1, PROCESSOR_WORKERS // 4)` | Number of Workload observation/training progress pool workers. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH` | `65536` (three roles) | `'10000'` | Regional cap on outstanding requests; routine traffic gets 429 first once it reaches the reserved line. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_MAX_CLUSTER_QUEUE_DEPTH` | `4096` (three roles) | `'1000'` | Cap on outstanding requests per cluster, preventing one GPU cluster dragging down the whole Region. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_FAULT_RESERVED_QUEUE_DEPTH` | `8192` (three roles) | `2/5 of PROCESSOR_MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH` | Capacity reserved globally for priority 0. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_FAULT_RESERVED_CLUSTER_DEPTH` | `512` (three roles) | `2/5 of PROCESSOR_MAX_CLUSTER_QUEUE_DEPTH` | Capacity reserved per cluster for priority 0. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_GLOBAL_ADMISSION_GUARD` | `256` (three roles) | `min(256, PROCESSOR_MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH)` | Cross-request concurrent admission gate; must not exceed the global queue depth. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` | `16777216` (three roles) | `16777216 (16 MiB)` | Hard cap on a single enqueue request body; 413 beyond it. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_ROUTINE_STARVATION_SECONDS` | worker=`30` | `'30'` | A routine P100 request waiting longer than this gets a temporary priority boost. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_NOTIFICATION_SHARDS` | worker=`24` | `<implicit>` | Number of advisory-lock shards for PostgreSQL queue notifications; the regional value matches 24 worker processes. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_NOTIFICATION_FALLBACK_SECONDS` | worker=`5` | `'5'` | Fallback polling cap while LISTEN/NOTIFY is healthy. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_CLEANUP_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | `60` (three roles) | `'60'` | Cleanup period for Processor tombstones, evidence and remote commands. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_CLEANUP_BATCH_SIZE` | `1000` (three roles) | `'1000'` | Maximum records per cleanup round; must be capacity-planned together with the production rate. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_COMPLETED_RETENTION_SECONDS` | `600` (three roles) | `'600'` | Retention of completed requests; a client resubmitting within it gets the same response. |

## 5. Processor Leases, Retries and Exit

These values jointly constrain request deadlines, lane takeover and retryable replay. The worker and ingress/spool lease/deadline differ; copying across roles is forbidden.

| Environment variable | Regional manifest value | Application default/requirement | Meaning and management advice |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_REQUEST_LEASE_SECONDS` | ingress=`30`<br>worker=`150`<br>spool=`30` | `'120'` | Request lane lease. Regional worker is 150s, ingress/spool 30s. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_REQUEST_RENEW_SECONDS` | ingress=`5`<br>worker=`10`<br>spool=`5` | `'5'` | Request lease renewal interval. Regional worker is 10s, ingress/spool 5s. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_REQUEST_MAX_EXECUTION_SECONDS` | ingress=`20`<br>worker=`120`<br>spool=`20` | `'30'` | Hard deadline of the business handler. Regional worker is 120s, ingress/spool 20s. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `115` (three roles) | `'115'` | Cap on the synchronous entry waiting for a Processor response; after a timeout query by request ID, it does not mean the request was lost. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_RETRYABLE_RESPONSE_MAX_AGE_SECONDS` | `300` (three roles) | `'300'` | Maximum event age for which 408/425/429/5xx is retryable; beyond it the poison queue is terminated. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_RETRY_AFTER_SECONDS` | `2` (three roles) | `'2'` | Suggested backoff seconds returned to clients on 429/503. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_RETRY_BACKOFF_SECONDS` | `1` (three roles) | `'1'` | Initial delay of a persistent retry, written into not_before. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_RETRY_BACKOFF_MAX_SECONDS` | `30` (three roles) | `'30'` | Exponential backoff cap; order is kept while a STRICT lane waits. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_COMPLETION_CLUSTER_CONCURRENCY` | worker=`1` | `'1'` | Parallelism of completion transactions across different clusters. Production is 1; 2/4 must first pass CAP-005. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_DRAIN_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS` | `30` (three roles) | `'30'` | Cap on an aggregate workflow waiting for same-cluster Processor requests to drain. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_EXIT_ON_DEADLINE` | `true` (three roles) | `<implicit>` | Whether a process exits and is recreated by Kubernetes when a request deadline runs away. Production keeps true. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_EXIT_GRACE_SECONDS` | `5` (three roles) | `'5'` | Wind-down time before an unhealthy process hard-exits. |
| `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_THREAD_DUMP_SIGNAL` | worker=`SIGUSR2` | `''` | Signal for capturing Processor thread stacks on site; regional production is SIGUSR2. |

## 6. Workflow, Executor and Remote Commands

Workflow owns the persistent state machine, the Cluster Executor owns execution inside the GPU cluster. Administrators mainly adjust scan frequency, concurrency and timeouts and should not bypass the Runtime Profile or the operation allowlist.

| Environment variable | Regional manifest value | Application default/requirement | Meaning and management advice |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GPU_FAULT_EXECUTOR_MODE` | `active` (three roles) | `'simulation'` | Execution mode. Only active performs real actions; simulation is for development and drills only. |
| `GPU_FAULT_ALLOWED_OPERATIONS` | Jointly constrained by the generated manifest and the Runtime Profile | `''` | Control-plane operation whitelist; being enumerated does not mean authorised, a unique owner and the downstream allowlist are still needed. |
| `GPU_FAULT_ENABLE_WORKFLOW_DISPATCHER` | ingress=`true`<br>worker=`true`<br>spool=`false` | `True` | Whether to start the workflow dispatcher; when off only state is saved and no action advances. |
| `GPU_FAULT_ENABLE_WORKFLOW_PREEMPTION` | `true` (three roles) | `True` | Allows a higher recovery rank to preempt a weaker workflow within the safety boundary. |
| `GPU_FAULT_WORKFLOW_LEASE_DURATION_SECONDS` | `180` (three roles) | `'180'` | Workflow execution lease; after expiry another worker increments the epoch and takes over. |
| `GPU_FAULT_WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | — | `'1800'` | Total cap on a whole workflow's execution; written into execution_deadline at first claim and enforced by the lease-holding executor itself. |
| `GPU_FAULT_WORKFLOW_STEP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | — | `'600'` | Cap on a single step staying non-terminal; beyond it the step becomes FAILED, independent of any adapter retry count. |
| `GPU_FAULT_WORKFLOW_STEP_WARNING_SECONDS` | — | `'300'` | How long a single step waits before alerting starts; must be less than the step cap, and affects only alerting, not the verdict. |
| `GPU_FAULT_WORKFLOW_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | `5` (three roles) | `'5'` | Fallback scan interval for persistent workflows; event completion also wakes it proactively. |
| `GPU_FAULT_WORKFLOW_BATCH_SIZE` | — | `'100'` | Cap on workflows per scan round. |
| `GPU_FAULT_WORKFLOW_DISPATCHER_WORKERS` | `8` (three roles) | `'8'` | Number of workflow execution threads per worker process. |
| `GPU_FAULT_DEFAULT_RESTART_BUDGET` | `1` (three roles) | `'1'` | Default automatic restart budget when the job declares none; persisted per cluster/job. |
| `GPU_FAULT_REMOTE_STEP_BATCHING` | `true` (three roles) | `True` | Consecutive node-side steps on the same node (QUIESCE/VERIFY/RESET/RESTORE/TRIGGER_HEALTH_SNAPSHOT) are merged into one compound remote command; default true, but it only really takes effect once the required/compatible pins no longer admit Executors with protocol <3. false restores one command per step. |
| `GPU_FAULT_REMOTE_COMMAND_CLAIM_DEADLINE_SECONDS` | — | `'900'` | Dead-letter time for a PENDING remote command unclaimed for a long time. |
| `GPU_FAULT_REMOTE_COMMAND_RETENTION_SECONDS` | — | `'86400'` | Retention of terminal remote commands. |

## 7. Fleet, Agent Compatibility and Cluster Executor

The required/compatible pins are the core of rolling upgrades. A candidate version first enters compatible and is promoted to required only after full convergence; do not clear the compatibility window by hand ahead of time.

| Environment variable | Regional manifest value | Application default/requirement | Meaning and management advice |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GPU_FAULT_ENABLE_AGENT_REGISTRY` | `true` (three roles) | `False` | Enables the Agent heartbeat registry and compatibility gate; must be on in regional production. |
| `GPU_FAULT_AGENT_MAX_HEARTBEAT_AGE_SECONDS` | `90` (three roles) | `'90'` | Maximum Agent heartbeat age; beyond it the node cannot execute actions. |
| `GPU_FAULT_AGENT_MAINTENANCE_WINDOW_SECONDS` | `420` (three roles) | `'420'` | Maintenance window after quiesce during which the same generation may pause heartbeats. |
| `GPU_FAULT_REQUIRED_AGENT_VERSION` | `0.10.0` (three roles) | `<implicit>` | Steady-state required Agent version; the actual release also checks artifact/config/protocol. |
| `GPU_FAULT_REQUIRED_AGENT_ARTIFACT_SHA256` | `ConfigMap gpu-fault-release-metadata/required-agent-artifact-sha256` (three roles) | `''` | Steady-state Node Runtime wheel SHA-256. |
| `GPU_FAULT_REQUIRED_AGENT_COMPATIBILITY_DIGEST` | `ConfigMap gpu-fault-release-metadata/required-agent-compatibility-digest` (three roles) | `<implicit>` | Agent behaviour compatibility digest. |
| `GPU_FAULT_REQUIRED_AGENT_CONFIG_DIGEST` | `ConfigMap gpu-fault-release-metadata/required-agent-config-digest` (three roles) | `''` | Digest of the configuration actually installed on nodes. |
| `GPU_FAULT_REQUIRED_AGENT_PROTOCOL_VERSION` | `ConfigMap gpu-fault-release-metadata/required-agent-protocol-version` (three roles) | `'3', str(CURRENT_AGENT_PROTOCOL_VERSION)` | Agent protocol version required by the control plane. |
| `GPU_FAULT_REQUIRED_REGIONAL_EXECUTOR_ARTIFACT_SHA256` | `ConfigMap gpu-fault-release-metadata/required-regional-executor-artifact-sha256` (three roles) | `''` | Steady-state Cluster Executor wheel SHA-256. |
| `GPU_FAULT_REQUIRED_REGIONAL_EXECUTOR_COMPATIBILITY_DIGEST` | `ConfigMap gpu-fault-release-metadata/required-regional-executor-compatibility-digest` (three roles) | `<implicit>` | Cluster Executor behaviour compatibility digest. |
| `GPU_FAULT_REQUIRED_REGIONAL_EXECUTOR_PROTOCOL_VERSION` | `ConfigMap gpu-fault-release-metadata/required-regional-executor-protocol-version` (three roles) | `'2', str(CURRENT_REGIONAL_EXECUTOR_PROTOCOL_VERSION)` | Regional Executor protocol version required by the control plane. |
| `GPU_FAULT_CLUSTER_EXECUTOR_MAX_CONCURRENT_COMMANDS` | — | `'5'` | Cap on commands one Executor handles concurrently; not a cluster-level remediation concurrency cap. |
| `GPU_FAULT_CLUSTER_EXECUTOR_LEASE_SECONDS` | — | `'120'` | Lease duration for an Executor claiming a remote command. |
| `GPU_FAULT_CLUSTER_EXECUTOR_POLL_SECONDS` | — | `'2'` | Idle interval when a command returns to WAITING, also the starting point of the backoff when the control plane is unreachable; with long polling on, empty answers no longer sleep by it. |
| `GPU_FAULT_CLUSTER_EXECUTOR_CLAIM_WAIT_SECONDS` | — | `'20'` | claim long poll: the maximum seconds the control plane holds an empty result (0–30, server cap 25); 0 disables and falls back to pure polling. |

## 8. Collector, DCGM and Inventory

Nodes enable the four systemd Collectors kernel, Fabric Manager, GPU metrics and host by default; NodeLog and the nvidia-smi fallback are off by default.

| Environment variable | Regional manifest value | Application default/requirement | Meaning and management advice |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GPU_FAULT_COLLECTOR_HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | — | `'10'` | Timeout of a single HTTP request from a Collector to the control plane. |
| `GPU_FAULT_COLLECTOR_OUTBOX_MAX_RECORDS` | — | `'1000'` | Maximum records in each Collector's local NDJSON outbox; not an indefinite queue. |
| `GPU_FAULT_COLLECTOR_OUTBOX_REPLAY_BUDGET_SECONDS` | — | `'5'` | Time budget per round for resubmitting backlog; real-time events take priority. |
| `GPU_FAULT_COLLECTOR_STARTUP_SPREAD_SECONDS` | — | `'15'` | Stagger window for the first sample after node start, avoiding the whole fleet hitting the control plane at once. |
| `GPU_FAULT_ENABLE_NODE_LOG_COLLECTOR` | false (current production keeps it disabled) | `<implicit>` | Enables the generic journal/training log Collector; needs independent capacity and privacy acceptance. |
| `GPU_FAULT_ENABLE_NVIDIA_SMI_METRICS_COLLECTOR` | false (limited fallback only when DCGM is unavailable) | `<implicit>` | Allows nvidia-smi to replace GPU metrics; lacks complete PCIe/NVLink/throttle signals. |
| `GPU_FAULT_DCGM_METRICS_URL` | Node systemd default http://127.0.0.1:9400/metrics | `'http://127.0.0.1:9400/metrics'` | DCGM Exporter endpoint read by the GPU metrics Collector. |
| `GPU_FAULT_DCGM_EDGE_FILTER_ENABLED` | — | `True` | Sends only baselines, health summaries, anomaly edges/recoveries and error deltas, lowering steady-state traffic. |
| `GPU_FAULT_DCGM_HEALTH_SUMMARY_SECONDS` | — | `'300'` | Period of the full GPU health summary when nothing changes. |
| `GPU_FAULT_DCGM_EDGE_CONFIRMATION_SAMPLES` | — | `'3'` | Number of consecutive confirmation samples for a candidate anomaly. |
| `GPU_FAULT_HOST_EDGE_FILTER_ENABLED` | — | `True` | Whether Host telemetry performs baseline/edge compression on the node side. |
| `GPU_FAULT_HOST_HEALTH_SUMMARY_SECONDS` | — | `'300'` | Period of the Host no-change health summary. |
| `GPU_FAULT_EXPECTED_GPU_COUNT` | Written by the node installer per instance type | `<implicit>` | Expected GPU count of this node; unknown instance types must be configured explicitly, not skipped silently. |
| `GPU_FAULT_EXPECTED_EFA_DEVICE_COUNT` | Written by the node installer per instance type | `<implicit>` | Expected EFA device count of this node. |
| `GPU_FAULT_GPU_INVENTORY_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | — | `'60'` | Independent GPU inventory reporting period. |
| `GPU_FAULT_GPU_INVENTORY_MAX_AGE_SECONDS` | — | `'180'` | Maximum GPU inventory age the control plane may use for recovery validation. |

## 9. Telemetry spool

The spool is an optional flood relief bypass. The base regional manifest by default does not let ingress write the spool, and the dedicated spool-worker, although configured enabled, has 0 replicas; when enabling, both ends must be adjusted together.

| Environment variable | Regional manifest value | Application default/requirement | Meaning and management advice |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GPU_FAULT_TELEMETRY_SPOOL` | ingress=`false`<br>spool=`true` | `False` | Whether the routine telemetry spool is enabled; scaling only the spool-worker produces no new spool data. |
| `GPU_FAULT_TELEMETRY_SPOOL_WORKERS` | spool=`8` | `2 × Processor default sub-pool` | Normal replay threads of a single spool-worker process. |
| `GPU_FAULT_TELEMETRY_SPOOL_MAX_DEPTH` | ingress=`65536` | `PROCESSOR_MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH` | Global admission depth cap of the spool. |
| `GPU_FAULT_TELEMETRY_SPOOL_MAX_CLUSTER_DEPTH` | ingress=`1024` | `PROCESSOR_MAX_CLUSTER_QUEUE_DEPTH` | Per-cluster spool depth cap. |
| `GPU_FAULT_TELEMETRY_SPOOL_MAX_ITEM_BYTES` | ingress=`4194304`<br>spool=`4194304` | `str(4 * 1024 * 1024)` | Byte cap for a single routine telemetry item entering the spool. |
| `GPU_FAULT_TELEMETRY_SPOOL_REPLAY_BATCH_MAX_BYTES` | spool=`8388608` | `str(8 * 1024 * 1024)` | Total byte cap of a single internal replay batch. |
| `GPU_FAULT_TELEMETRY_SPOOL_MAX_IN_FLIGHT_BYTES` | spool=`67108864` | `str(64 * 1024 * 1024)` | Total in-flight byte cap of all replay futures in one process. |
| `GPU_FAULT_TELEMETRY_SPOOL_RETRY_BACKOFF_SECONDS` | spool=`1` | `'1'` | Base backoff seconds after a spool replay failure. |

## 10. Node Agent, Destructive Actions and Diagnostics

Node actions need the control-plane allowlist, Runtime Profile, Node Agent allowlist, signature and fencing to pass at the same time. Turning on a node switch does not automatically grant execution authorisation.

| Environment variable | Regional manifest value | Application default/requirement | Meaning and management advice |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GPU_FAULT_NODE_AGENT_PORT` | — | `'9099'` | Node Agent listening port, regional default 9099. |
| `GPU_FAULT_NODE_ALLOWED_OPERATIONS` | Generated by the node installer from approved capabilities | `'VERIFY_NO_GPU_CLIENTS'` | Final Node Agent operation allowlist; a missing entry refuses the corresponding action. |
| `GPU_FAULT_NODE_ALLOW_GPU_RESET` | Explicitly true in the current regional installation | `False` | Allows signed GPU reset; still needs no clients, quiesce, fencing and post-action validation. |
| `GPU_FAULT_NODE_ALLOW_FABRIC_RESET` | Explicitly true in the current regional installation | `False` | Allows all-GPU/NVSwitch reset; must have complete inventory and barrier. |
| `GPU_FAULT_NODE_ALLOW_SERVICE_QUIESCE` | Explicitly true in the current regional installation | `False` | Allows quiescing/restoring GPU services; on failure the fail-safe timer restores automatically. |
| `GPU_FAULT_NODE_ALLOW_FABRIC_MANAGER_RESTART` | Explicitly true in the current regional installation | `False` | Allows a controlled Fabric Manager restart with verification of the new PID/active state. |
| `GPU_FAULT_QUIESCE_FAILSAFE_SECONDS` | — | `'420'` | Fail-safe cap for automatic restore after service quiesce, preventing an Agent/control-plane disconnect leaving a node out of service. |
| `GPU_FAULT_DEVICE_SWEEP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | — | `'20'` | Total timeout for sweeping GPU clients and the process tree. |
| `GPU_FAULT_DIAGNOSTIC_OUTPUT_DIR` | — | `'/var/lib/gpu-fault/diagnostics'` | Directory for node diagnostic bundles and command output. |
| `GPU_FAULT_DIAGNOSTIC_S3_URI` | — | `<implicit>` | Optional diagnostic object storage prefix; when empty file:// evidence is readable only locally on the faulty node. |
| `GPU_FAULT_FIELD_DIAGNOSTIC_COMMAND` | — | `''` | Site-approved absolute path of the Field Diagnostic command; empty means disabled. |
| `GPU_FAULT_FIELD_DIAGNOSTIC_SHA256` | — | `<implicit>` | Pinned SHA-256 of the Field Diagnostic command/tool. |
| `GPU_FAULT_DRIVER_REMEDIATION_COMMAND` | — | `''` | Site-approved driver remediation command; must be configured together with the target version and SHA. |
| `GPU_FAULT_DRIVER_REMEDIATION_SHA256` | — | `<implicit>` | Pinned SHA-256 of the driver remediation command. |

## 11. HyperPod, reboot and warm spare

Provider replace is permanently forbidden. nodeReplace only means HEALTHY_WARM_SPARE_ONLY; reboot and warm-spare must be approved and accepted separately.

| Environment variable | Regional manifest value | Application default/requirement | Meaning and management advice |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GPU_FAULT_ENABLE_HYPERPOD_ADAPTER` | `false` (three roles) | `False` | Enables the HyperPod lifecycle adapter; used by the regional data-plane Executor. |
| `GPU_FAULT_HYPERPOD_CLUSTER` | Real HyperPod name injected by each cluster's connection Secret | `<implicit>` | Provider cluster name; different from the stable cluster_id. |
| `GPU_FAULT_HYPERPOD_CONFIRM_CLUSTER` | Must exactly equal the real HyperPod name | `''` | Second cluster confirmation for destructive provider actions. |
| `GPU_FAULT_ALLOW_HYPERPOD_REBOOT` | true (after phase D.1 approval) | `legacy_mutation_enabled` | Allows BatchRebootClusterNodes without destroying instances. |
| `GPU_FAULT_ALLOW_HYPERPOD_REPLACE` | false (solution invariant; startup fails when true) | `False` | Provider replace master switch; must always be false, warm-spare does not depend on it. |
| `GPU_FAULT_ALLOW_WITH_AUTOMATIC_NODE_RECOVERY` | false (solution invariant) | `False` | Forbids mutations under NodeRecovery=Automatic. |
| `GPU_FAULT_ENABLE_HYPERPOD_MANAGED_OBSERVER` | ingress=`true`<br>worker=`true`<br>spool=`false` | `True` | Read-only observation of HyperPod node state and provider outcome. |
| `GPU_FAULT_ENABLE_HYPERPOD_SPARE_FAILOVER` | true (HEALTHY_WARM_SPARE_ONLY path only) | `False` | Enables local failover to customer-provided warm spares; not a provider replace authorisation. |
| `GPU_FAULT_HYPERPOD_SPARE_LABEL` | `gpu-fault.io/spare` (three roles) | `'gpu-fault.io/spare'` | Kubernetes label key identifying warm-spare nodes. |
| `GPU_FAULT_HYPERPOD_SPARE_LABEL_VALUE` | `true` (three roles) | `'true'` | Expected value of the warm-spare label. |
| `GPU_FAULT_HYPERPOD_POST_REBOOT_STABILIZATION_SECONDS` | `60` (three roles) | `'60'` | Wait after reboot for the device plugin/Agent to stabilise before validating. |
| `GPU_FAULT_HYPERPOD_MAX_BATCH_SIZE` | — | `'25'` | Maximum nodes per provider mutation. |
| `GPU_FAULT_HYPERPOD_IDENTITY_REFRESH_SECONDS` | `20` (three roles) | `'20'` | Refresh period of HyperPod NodeLogicalId/instance identity. |

## 12. Notifications, Evidence and Retention

Business notifications go through the Aurora outbox and are then sent by the dispatcher to the site SNS topic (default channel=sns, sharing one topic and one subscription confirmation mail with AMP metric alerts), or via SES per the site declaration (channel=ses). A notification being QUEUED does not equal delivered; SENT and the provider message ID must be seen.

| Environment variable | Regional manifest value | Application default/requirement | Meaning and management advice |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GPU_FAULT_ACKNOWLEDGE_NO_ALERT_CHANNEL` | false (must not be enabled in production) | `<implicit>` | Whether to only record when there is no outbound notification channel. Emergency compatibility only; production keeps false. |
| `GPU_FAULT_NOTIFICATION_CHANNEL` | Rendered from spec.notifications.channel of site.yaml (new sites sns) | `<implicit>` | Business notification channel: sns (site SNS topic, plain text), ses (verified sender identity) or disabled (store only). When undeclared inferred as topic ARN present → sns, SES address pair present → ses. |
| `GPU_FAULT_SNS_TOPIC_ARN` | Rendered from spec.health.snsTopicArn of site.yaml | `<implicit>` | SNS topic ARN for publishing business notifications when channel=sns; the control-plane role holds sns:Publish only on it. |
| `GPU_FAULT_ALLOW_EMAIL` | `true` (three roles) | `False, True` | Whether business notifications (SNS or SES) are actually sent. Default true when channel=sns; false is the master valve. |
| `GPU_FAULT_EMAIL_SENDER` | Injected from the verified SES identity of site.yaml when channel=ses | `<implicit>` | SES sender identity, used only when channel=ses; three separate concepts from the administrator contact and the recipient list. |
| `GPU_FAULT_EMAIL_RECIPIENTS` | Injected from emailRecipients of site.yaml when channel=ses | `''` | Comma-separated business notification recipient list, used only when channel=ses. |
| `GPU_FAULT_EMAIL_SUBJECT_PREFIX` | `Secret gpu-fault-email/email-subject-prefix` (three roles) | `''` | Mail environment/site prefix, not a substitute for site, Region, account and cluster in the body. |
| `GPU_FAULT_SES_CONFIGURATION_SET` | Rendered from spec.notifications.sesConfigurationSet of site.yaml when channel=ses, empty when undeclared | `<implicit>` | SES v2 configuration set name, used only when channel=ses; explicitly cleared when undeclared. Rendered from the checked site configuration, not inherited from the shell running deploy. |
| `GPU_FAULT_NOTIFICATION_ASYNC_DELIVERY` | `true` (three roles) | `False` | Whether delivery goes into the persistent outbox; regional production is true. |
| `GPU_FAULT_NOTIFICATION_DISPATCHER_ENABLED` | `true` (three roles) | `False` | Whether to start the notification dispatcher; when off, store only, no sending. |
| `GPU_FAULT_NOTIFICATION_LEASE_SECONDS` | `120` (three roles) | `'120'` | Notification delivery lease; an old epoch must not complete a new lease. |
| `GPU_FAULT_NOTIFICATION_BATCH_SIZE` | `25` (three roles) | `'25'` | Cap on notifications claimed per round. |
| `GPU_FAULT_NOTIFICATION_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | `8` (three roles) | `'8'` | Maximum delivery attempts per notification. |
| `GPU_FAULT_NOTIFICATION_TTL_SECONDS` | — | `str(DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_TTL_SECONDS)` | Generic notification shelf life; a category can be overridden individually with the dynamic variable family. |
| `GPU_FAULT_EVIDENCE_RETENTION_HOURS` | `24` (three roles) | `'24'` | Default retention hours of control-plane raw evidence. |
| `GPU_FAULT_EVIDENCE_MAX_RECORDS_PER_NODE` | `10000` (three roles) | `'10000'` | Cap on raw evidence records per node. |
| `GPU_FAULT_METRICS_WORKFLOW_SCAN_WINDOW_SECONDS` | — | `'604800'` | Time window (seconds) of terminal workflows in the /metrics detail scan: non-terminal workflows are read however old, terminal ones only with updated_at inside the window; the step, duration and milestone families therefore describe only closed loops within the window. 0 disables the window and falls back to the latest N rows, making GpuFaultWorkflowMetricScanTruncated fire by table size rather than in-flight count. |
| `GPU_FAULT_METRICS_WORKFLOW_SCAN_LIMIT` | — | `'20000'` | Hard row cap of the /metrics detail scan, applying to the union of non-terminal and in-window terminal; beyond it gpu_fault_workflow_scan_truncated is set. Raising it only shifts cost to Aurora and every scrape; first deal with the source producing workflows. |
| `GPU_FAULT_CONTROL_RECORD_RETENTION_DAYS` | — | `'0'` | incident/workflow archive-first retention days; bare process default 0 = off, site default 30 days, only an explicit 0 disables. Rendered from the checked site configuration spec.retention.controlRecordRetentionDays, enters only the control-worker, not set directly online. |
| `GPU_FAULT_CONTROL_RECORD_ARCHIVE_S3_URI` | — | `''` | archive-first target S3 URI (required when retention days >0); write the archive and verify the SHA first, then delete live rows. From site.yaml spec.retention.archiveS3Uri; deploy also grants the control-plane role s3:PutObject on that prefix. |
| `GPU_FAULT_CONTROL_RECORD_ARCHIVE_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | — | `'600'` | Control record archive scan period; from site.yaml spec.retention.archiveIntervalSeconds, default 3600. |
| `GPU_FAULT_CONTROL_RECORD_ARCHIVE_BATCH_SIZE` | 200 | `'200'` | Maximum incidents processed per archive scan round; ≤0 errors. A single archive failure counts in errors_total and continues without aborting the round. |
| `GPU_FAULT_MARKER_RETENTION_SECONDS` | — | `'2592000'` | Retention seconds of inactive markers (default 30 days); ≤0 disables cleanup. Markers whose incident still exists are not deleted and are packaged with the archiver. |
| `GPU_FAULT_NOTIFICATION_RETENTION_SECONDS` | — | `'2592000'` | Retention seconds of terminal notification records (default 30 days); ≤0 disables cleanup. Not deleted while delivery is still PENDING/RETRY/LEASED or the incident still exists. |
| `GPU_FAULT_COMPLETION_RECORD_RETENTION_SECONDS` | — | `'2592000'` | Retention seconds of completion event/decision records (default 30 days); ≤0 disables cleanup. Not deleted while still referenced by an incident. |
| `GPU_FAULT_REGISTRY_MEMBER_RETENTION_SECONDS` | — | `'86400'` | Retention seconds of regional registry member heartbeat records (default 1 day); ≤0 disables cleanup. Only regional roles run this sweep. |
| `GPU_FAULT_REMOTE_COMMAND_STALE_FENCE_GRACE_SECONDS` | 600 | `'600'` | Grace seconds after a LEASED remote command's lease expires before a command whose fence no longer matches is swept to FAILED(stale-fence) (D-9). |

## Dynamic Variable Families

| Pattern | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `GPU_FAULT_NOTIFICATION_TTL_SECONDS_<CATEGORY>` | Overrides the shelf life per notification category; the generic notification TTL is used when unset. |
| `GPU_FAULT_FLEET_<FIELD>` | Temporary context passed by the fleet CLI to the transport subprocess, not persistent administrator configuration. |

Variables not appearing in this document are by default considered developer or component-internal configuration; when adjustment is needed first look up
the using module in the [complete Environment Variable Reference](environment-variables-reference.md), then
modify the generated source of truth per [Developer Deployment Implementation](developer-deployment-implementation.md).
